questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 50° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of two supplementary angles is always 180°.

Smaller angle = (Sum of angles − Difference) ÷ 2

Smaller angle = (180° − 50°) ÷ 2

Smaller angle = 130° ÷ 2 = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two angles are supplementary.

The larger angle is 50° more than the smaller angle.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of supplementary angles = 180°

 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 
 

 x

 
 

 x + 50°

 
 

 180°

**Calculations:**

Let the smaller angle be x.

⇒ Larger angle = x + 50°

⇒ x + (x + 50°) = 180°

⇒ 2x + 50° = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 50°

⇒ 2x = 130°

⇒ x = 130° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is exactly 180°. When placed adjacent to each other, they form a straight line.

Complementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is exactly 90°. For example, 40° and 50° form a complementary pair.

Adjacent Angles

Angles that share a common vertex and a common boundary side, but have no overlapping interior area.

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two straight lines intersect, the non-adjacent opposite angles formed are always equal.
</p

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 17 cm, BC = 8 cm, CD = 9 cm, AD = 12 cm, and AC = 15 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Diagonal AC divides the quadrilateral into two right-angled triangles: ΔABC and ΔADC.

In ΔABC (sides 8 cm, 15 cm, 17 cm), 8² + 15² = 17² ⇒ Area = (1/2) × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

In ΔADC (sides 9 cm, 12 cm, 15 cm), 9² + 12² = 15² ⇒ Area = (1/2) × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².

Total Area = Area of ΔABC + Area of ΔADC = 60 + 54 = 114 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 114 cm².**

questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 28° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two angles with a given sum and difference, Smaller angle = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2.

The sum of supplementary angles is always 180°.

⇒ Smaller angle = (180° − 28°) ÷ 2

⇒ Smaller angle = 152° ÷ 2 = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two angles are supplementary.

The larger angle is 28° more than the smaller angle.

**Concept Used:**

The sum of two supplementary angles is always 180°.

 
• 
 
 
• 
 
 

 
 

 
 x
 x + 28°
 
 

 Sum = 180° (Supplementary Angles)
 

**Calculation:**

Let the smaller angle be x.

⇒ Larger angle = x + 28°

According to the concept of supplementary angles:

⇒ x + (x + 28°) = 180°

⇒ 2x + 28° = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 28°

⇒ 2x = 152°

⇒ x = 152° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to exactly 180°. They form a straight line when placed adjacent to each other.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their combined sum equals exactly 90°, forming a right angle.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a straight line, then the sum of the two adjacent angles so formed is exactly 180°.
</p

questions.question: What is the ratio of the angles subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle to the angle subtended at any point on the circumference of the circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the standard **degree measure theorem** of circles, the angle subtended by an arc or chord at the **centre** is always twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the **circumference**.

Let the angle subtended at the circumference be θ.

Then, the angle subtended at the centre is 2θ.

Required Ratio = Angle at Centre : Angle at Circumference = 2θ : θ = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ A circle with **centre O**.

⇒ A **chord AB** subtending an angle ∠AOB at the centre **O**.

⇒ The same chord subtends an angle ∠ACB at point **C** on the circumference.

**Theorem Used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the circumference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/065a2d93c669ae2b48f6c0f63f2e98335f0c24d6f81008d7abc12f7638591eca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angle subtended at the circumference be ∠ACB = θ

⇒ According to the theorem, the angle subtended at the centre is ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2θ

⇒ Required Ratio = ∠AOB : ∠ACB

⇒ Ratio = 2θ : θ

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**Explanation of Incorrect Options:**

⇒ **Option (1) 3 : 1** is incorrect because the central angle is exactly double, not triple, the inscribed angle.

⇒ **Option (2) 1 : 3** is incorrect because the central angle must be larger than the inscribed angle, making a ratio less than 1 impossible.

⇒ **Option (3) 1 : 2** is incorrect because this represents the ratio of the angle at the circumference to the angle at the centre, which is the reverse of the requested order.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

An angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°), which is half of the 180° straight angle at the centre.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment of the circumference are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral always sum up to 180° (they are supplementary).</p

questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 56°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 32° and ∠GFE = 47°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

∠BEF = 180° − ∠PEB = 180° − 56° = 124° (Linear pair)

∠GEF = ∠BEF − ∠BEG = 124° − 32° = 92°

In ▵EGF, sum of angles = 180°

∠EGF = 180° − (∠GEF + ∠GFE) = 180° − (92° + 47°) = 41°

**∴ The correct answer is 41°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB || CD**, **transversal PQ** intersects them at **E** and **F**. **∠PEB = 56°**, **∠BEG = 32°**, and **∠GFE = 47°**.

**Formula Used:** Linear pair property (sum = 180°) and Angle Sum Property of a triangle (sum = 180°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21336634dfba58e0dee75adbbf3b46c458b1026b3ada460dbda6252dfd3093f1.png] 

⇒ Since **PQ** is a straight line, **∠PEB + ∠BEF = 180°** (Linear pair)

⇒ 56° + ∠BEF = 180°

⇒ ∠BEF = 180° − 56° = 124°

⇒ From the figure, **∠BEF = ∠BEG + ∠GEF**

⇒ 124° = 32° + ∠GEF

⇒ ∠GEF = 124° − 32° = 92°

⇒ In **▵EGF**, **∠GEF + ∠GFE + ∠EGF = 180°**

⇒ 92° + 47° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ 139° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − 139° = 41°

**∴ The correct answer is 41°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal, and alternate interior angles are equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.</p

questions.question: ABCD is a trapezium in which BC ∥ AD and AC = CD. If ∠ABC = 69° and ∠BAC = 23° , then what is the measure of ∠ACD (in degree) .?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In ΔABC, the sum of angles is 180°.

∠ACB = 180° − (∠ABC + ∠BAC) = 180° − (69° + 23°) = 88°.

Since **BC ∥ AD**, alternate interior angles are equal: ∠CAD = ∠ACB = 88°.

In ΔACD, since **AC = CD**, we have ∠ADC = ∠CAD = 88°.

Therefore, ∠ACD = 180° − (∠CAD + ∠ADC) = 180° − (88° + 88°) = 4°.

**∴ The correct answer is 4°.**

questions.question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S, respectively. If ∠BRP = (2x + 13)° and ∠DSP = (3x − 22)°, then find ∠CSP.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify that ∠BRP and ∠DSP are **corresponding angles**, which are equal for **parallel lines**.

Equate the expressions: 2x + 13 = 3x − 22 ⇒ x = 35.

Calculate ∠DSP = 3(35) − 22 = 83°.

Since ∠CSP and ∠DSP form a **linear pair** on line CD, their sum is 180°.

∠CSP = 180° − 83° = 97°.

**∴ The correct answer is 97°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Line **AB || CD** and **PQ** is a **transversal**.

∠BRP = (2x + 13)° and ∠DSP = (3x − 22)°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Corresponding Angles:** When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the corresponding angles are equal.

2. **Linear Pair:** The sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d53e407b085c167c5e358bf851c06d37a9b907ebbf1f240510f0007e1a953f2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **AB || CD**, ∠BRP = ∠DSP (**Corresponding angles**)

⇒ 2x + 13 = 3x − 22

⇒ 13 + 22 = 3x − 2x

⇒ x = 35

⇒ Now, ∠DSP = 3(35) − 22

⇒ ∠DSP = 105 − 22 = 83°

⇒ On the straight line **CD**, ∠CSP + ∠DSP = 180° (**Linear pair**)

⇒ ∠CSP + 83° = 180°

⇒ ∠CSP = 180° − 83°

⇒ ∠CSP = 97°

**∴ The correct answer is 97°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines are equal (e.g., ∠ARS = ∠DSR).

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal and between the parallel lines are supplementary (sum = 180°).

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal.</p

questions.question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 22°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 36°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **ΔBDC**, since **BD ⊥ AC**, **∠C** = 90° − **∠DBC** = 90° − 22° = 68°.

In **ΔAEC**, **∠AEB** is the **exterior angle** at vertex **E** because **B, E, C** are collinear.

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem**, **∠AEB** = **∠CAE** + **∠C**.

⇒ **∠AEB** = 36° + 68° = 104°.

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In **ΔABC**, **BD ⊥ AC** at **D**, **∠DBC = 22°**, and **∠CAE = 36°** where **E** is on **BC**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Linear pair of angles sum to 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92a773a45eb75167a03a926a5a75ba56d37225184ce2f5a1a86469ac174e22a6.png] 

In **ΔBDC**:

⇒ **∠BDC** = 90° (Since **BD ⊥ AC**)

⇒ **∠BCD** + **∠DBC** + **∠BDC** = 180°

⇒ **∠BCD** + 22° + 90° = 180°

⇒ **∠BCD** = 180° − 112° = 68°

In **ΔAEC**:

⇒ **∠CAE** = 36° (Given)

⇒ **∠ACE** = **∠BCD** = 68°

⇒ **∠AEC** = 180° − (**∠CAE** + **∠ACE**)

⇒ **∠AEC** = 180° − (36° + 68°) = 180° − 104° = 76°

Since **B, E, C** lie on a straight line:

⇒ **∠AEB** + **∠AEC** = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ **∠AEB** = 180° − 76° = 104°

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then the measures of the angles add up to 180°.</p

questions.question: If ∆ ABC ∼ ∆ XYZ, AB = 6 cm, XY = 8 cm, YZ = 12 cm and ZX = 16 cm, then find the perimeter of ∆ ABC.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **Δ ABC ∼ Δ XYZ**, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of corresponding sides = AB ÷ XY = 6 ÷ 8 = 3 ÷ 4

**Perimeter of Δ XYZ** = XY + YZ + ZX = 8 + 12 + 16 = 36 cm

**Perimeter of Δ ABC** = (3 ÷ 4) × 36 = 27 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 27 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB = 6 cm, XY = 8 cm, YZ = 12 cm, ZX = 16 cm

**Δ ABC ∼ Δ XYZ**

**Formula Used:**

For **similar triangles**, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides:

AB ÷ XY = BC ÷ YZ = CA ÷ ZX = Perimeter(Δ ABC) ÷ Perimeter(Δ XYZ)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09614f69641a7a2b3ce5bf219bf62acd439bc0412752202056fdf152872a8391.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of Δ XYZ = XY + YZ + ZX

⇒ Perimeter of Δ XYZ = 8 + 12 + 16 = 36 cm

⇒ Since Δ ABC ∼ Δ XYZ, we have:

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC ÷ Perimeter of Δ XYZ = AB ÷ XY

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC ÷ 36 = 6 ÷ 8

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC ÷ 36 = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC = (3 ÷ 4) × 36

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC = 3 × 9 = 27 cm

**Explanation of incorrect options:**

**Option (1) 34 cm:** Incorrect, as the perimeter must be exactly 27 cm based on the similarity ratio of 3/4.

**Option (2) 24 cm:** Incorrect, as 24 cm would correspond to a similarity ratio of 2/3, which does not match AB/XY = 6/8 = 3/4.

**Option (4) 32 cm:** Incorrect, as 32 cm does not satisfy the similarity ratio of 3/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their perimeters, altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors.

Area Ratio Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ ABC) ÷ Area(Δ XYZ) = (AB ÷ XY)².

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy Angle-Angle (AA), Side-Angle-Side (SAS), or Side-Side-Side (SSS) similarity conditions.</p

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 250% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **exterior angles** of any convex polygon is always 360°.

Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + 250% of 360° = 3.5 × 360° = 1260°.

Using the formula (n − 2) × 180° = 1260° ⇒ n − 2 = 7 ⇒ n = 9.

For a **regular polygon**, each interior angle x = 1260° ÷ 9 = 140°.

**∴ The correct answer is 140°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of interior angles is 250% more than the sum of exterior angles.

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°; Sum of exterior angles = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d4280ebc0cc7383c05292b316685e53a459a5a926f97b28492e4a23c64ed040.png] 

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = 360°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + (250/100) × 360°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + 900° = 126

questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 49°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 35° and ∠GFE = 16°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **AB || CD**, the **linear pair** at point E gives ∠FEB = 180° − 49° = 131°.

The interior angle ∠FEG = ∠FEB − ∠BEG = 131° − 35° = 96°.

In **▵EFG**, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − (∠FEG + ∠GFE) = 180° − (96° + 16°) = 68°.

**∴ The correct answer is 68°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Line **AB || CD**, transversal **PQ** intersects them at E and F.

∠PEB = 49°, ∠BEG = 35°, and ∠GFE = 16°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

2. **Angle Sum Property:** Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d348b68bfe55688188bd6bd1fbd9732b10acc22425996638827d90350006367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since P-E-F-Q is a straight line, ∠PEB + ∠FEB = 180°

⇒ 49° + ∠FEB = 180°

⇒ ∠FEB = 180° − 49° = 131°

⇒ From the figure, ∠FEB = ∠FEG + ∠BEG

⇒ 131° = ∠FEG + 35°

⇒ ∠FEG = 131° − 35° = 96°

⇒ In **▵EFG**, ∠EGF + ∠FEG + ∠GFE = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF + 96° + 16° = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF + 112° = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − 112° = 68°

**∴ The correct answer is 68°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, **alternate interior angles** are equal, and **consecutive interior angles** are supplementary (sum to 180°).

Triangle Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

A linear pair is a set of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines; their measures always add up to 180°.</p

questions.question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal, such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S. If ∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y° and ∠DSP = 4x°, then find the values of x and y, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **PQ** is a straight line, **∠ARP** and **∠ARQ** form a **linear pair**, so 2x + y = 180.

For **parallel lines** **AB** and **CD**, the **exterior angle** ∠ARP and the **interior angle** ∠RSD are **corresponding angles** (thus equal).

Since **∠RSD** and **∠DSP** form a **linear pair** at point **S**, their sum is 180°.

Substituting **∠ARP** for **∠RSD**: 2x + 4x = 180 ⇒ 6x = 180 ⇒ **x = 30**.

Now, 2(30) + y = 180 ⇒ 60 + y = 180 ⇒ **y = 120**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30; 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**AB || CD** and **PQ** is a **transversal**.

∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y°, and ∠DSP = 4x°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

2. **Corresponding Angles Postulate:** If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, then the pairs of corresponding angles are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67166ceacd95e7441b95b3afbd31eb6d4d84c635d66cd35ef4be2b9cc1484f73.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **P-R-Q** is a straight line, ∠ARP + ∠ARQ = 180°

⇒ 2x + y = 180° --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Since **AB || CD**, ∠ARP = ∠RSC (**Corresponding angles**)

⇒ ∠RSC = 2x°

⇒ Now, at point **S**, ∠RSC + ∠DSP = 180° (**Linear pair**)

⇒ 2x + 4x = 180°

⇒ 6x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 6 = 30°

⇒ Substitute x = 30 in Equation 1:

⇒ 2(30) + y = 180°

⇒ 60 + y = 180°

⇒ y = 180° − 60° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 30; 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, angles in the same relative position at each intersection are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal are equal (e.g., ∠BRS = ∠RSC).

Co-interior Angles

Interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180°.</p

questions.question: Two concentric circles have radii of 10 cm and 26 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that is tangent to the smaller circle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **concentric circles**, the length of the **chord** of the larger circle that is **tangent** to the smaller circle is given by:

Length of chord = 2 × √(R² − r²)

Where R = 26 cm and r = 10 cm.

⇒ Length = 2 × √(26² − 10²) = 2 × √(676 − 100)

⇒ Length = 2 × √576 = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the larger circle (R) = 26 cm

Radius of the smaller circle (r) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **right-angled triangle**, Pythagoras theorem states: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/076a612dbba0d906778c406993fb63ecb600b4c9abefabe8304b1731c2f0318a.png] 

Let the two **concentric circles** have a common center O.

Let AB be the **chord** of the larger circle which is **tangent** to the smaller circle at point M.

Since OM is the radius of the smaller circle and AB is the tangent, OM ⊥ AB.

⇒ In right-angled ▵OMA, OA = 26 cm (Radius of larger circle) and OM = 10 cm (Radius of smaller circle).

Using **Pythagoras theorem** in ▵OMA:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 26² = 10² + AM²

⇒ 676 = 100 + AM²

⇒ AM² = 676 − 100 = 576

⇒ AM = √576 = 24 cm

Since the perpendicular from the center to a chord **bisects** the chord:

⇒ AB = 2 × AM = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentric Circles

Circles that share the same center but have different radii are called concentric circles.

Tangent-Radius Property

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact (OM ⊥ AB).

Chord Bisector Theorem

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord into two equal parts.</p

questions.question: A chord AB is drawn in a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. If the shortest distance between the centre and the chord is 4.5 cm, then find the length of chord AB.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Length of **chord AB** = 2 × √(**Radius**² − **Distance**²)

⇒ AB = 2 × √(6² − 4.5²)

⇒ AB = 2 × √(36 − 20.25)

⇒ AB = 2 × √15.75 = 2 × √(63/4)

⇒ AB = 2 × (3√7 / 2) = 3√7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√7 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Radius (OA)** = 6 cm, **Shortest distance (OM)** = 4.5 cm.

**Formula Used:** In a **right-angled triangle**, **Hypotenuse²** = **Base²** + **Perpendicular²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56cc96408308a650f72ec3d569ba79e0b85179ed05a1b8a680a794b6178fb4ec.png] 

In **right-angled triangle OMA**, where **M** is the midpoint of **chord AB**:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 6² = 4.5² + AM²

⇒ 36 = 20.25 + AM²

⇒ AM² = 36 − 20.25 = 15.75

⇒ AM = √15.75 = √(63/4) = 3√7 / 2 cm

Since the **perpendicular** from the **centre** bisects the **chord**:

⇒ AB = 2 × AM

⇒ AB = 2 × (3√7 / 2) = 3√7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√7 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

The **perpendicular** drawn from the **centre** of a circle to a **chord** always bisects the chord into two equal parts.

Pythagorean Relation in Circles

For any circle, the **radius (r)**, the **distance from the centre (d)**, and the **chord length (L)** are related by: r² = d² + (L/2)².

Shortest Distance

The **shortest distance** between a point (centre) and a line (chord) is always the **perpendicular distance**.</p

questions.question: If a transversal line intersects a pair of two parallel lines, then each pair of corresponding angles are:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the angles in matching corners are called **corresponding angles**.

By the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**, these angles are always equal in measure.

**∴ The correct answer is equal.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two parallel lines **m** and **n** intersected by a transversal line **t**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16f69bbcc252f3bbb492ece4638a9cefa5c623f9f35dfcf60c1c8ad5ab9782ab.png] 

**Theorem and Properties:**

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines:

⇒ **Corresponding angles** lie on the same side of the transversal and in the same relative position relative to the parallel lines (such as angle 1 and angle 2 in the diagram).

⇒ According to the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**, these angles are equal in measure.

**Analysis of Options:**

⇒ **Option 1 (Complementary):** Complementary angles sum up to 90°. Corresponding angles are not necessarily complementary unless the transversal is perpendicular to the parallel lines.

⇒ **Option 2 (Unequal):** Since the lines are parallel, the corresponding angles must be equal, not unequal.

⇒ **Option 3 (Equal):** This is the correct property of corresponding angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal.

⇒ **Option 4 (Supplementary):** Supplementary angles sum up to 180°. Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, but corresponding angles are equal.

**∴ The correct answer is equal.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles on opposite sides of the transversal and inside the parallel lines are always equal in measure.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal and inside the parallel lines are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180°.

Vertically Opposite Angles

Angles opposite to each other at the intersection of two lines are always equal, regardless of whether the lines are parallel.</p

questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 42°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 21° and ∠GFE = 34°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Calculate the interior angle ∠FEG = 180° − ∠PEB − ∠BEG = 180° − 42° − 21° = 117°.

In ▵EGF, the sum of angles is 180°.

∴ ∠EGF = 180° − (∠FEG + ∠GFE) = 180° − (117° + 34°) = 29°.

**∴ The correct answer is 29°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Parallel lines:** AB || CD

**Transversal:** PQ intersects AB at E and CD at F

**Angles:** ∠PEB = 42°, ∠BEG = 21°, ∠GFE = 34°

**Formula Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

2. **Angle Sum Property:** Sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53882011de10bd383bc40517fac682d94638b1caae89ec92964f01acab8280ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since PQ is a straight line, ∠PEB + ∠BEF = 180° (**Linear Pair**)

⇒ 42° + ∠BEF = 180°

⇒ ∠BEF = 180° − 42° = 138°

⇒ Now, ∠BEF = ∠BEG + ∠FEG

⇒ 138° = 21° + ∠FEG

⇒ ∠FEG = 138° − 21° = 117°

⇒ In **▵EGF**, by **Angle Sum Property**:

⇒ ∠FEG + ∠GFE + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ 117° + 34° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ 151° + ∠EGF = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − 151° = 29°

**∴ The correct answer is 29°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, **corresponding angles** are equal, and **alternate interior angles** are equal.

Consecutive Interior Angles

The sum of **consecutive interior angles** on the same side of a transversal is always 180°.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The **exterior angle** of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.</p

questions.question: Find the co-ordinates of the centroid of a triangle whose vertices are A(1, 4), B(7, 8) and C(10, 12).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **centroid** of a triangle is the **arithmetic mean** of the coordinates of its three vertices.

x-coordinate = (1 + 7 + 10) ÷ 3 = 6

y-coordinate = (4 + 8 + 12) ÷ 3 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is (6, 8).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices of the triangle are **A(1, 4)**, **B(7, 8)**, and **C(10, 12)**.

**Formula Used:** The coordinates of the **centroid** G(x, y) of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) are given by:

G(x, y) = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be106656760133ed639191f8c555850a681ea20e85e0b36f3ccad17f63eba7fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = (1 + 7 + 10) ÷ 3

⇒ x = 18 ÷ 3 = 6

⇒ y = (4 + 8 + 12) ÷ 3

⇒ y = 24 ÷ 3 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is (6, 8).**

**__Additional Information__**

Centroid Definition

The **centroid** is the point where the three **medians** of a triangle intersect. It is the geometric center of the triangle.

Median Ratio Property

The **centroid** divides each **median** in the ratio **2 : 1**, measured from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Area Property

The three **medians** divide the triangle into six smaller triangles, all of which have **equal area**.</p

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 46°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. What is the measure of ∠DOC?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the **angle bisectors** of two adjacent angles in a **quadrilateral** is always equal to half the sum of the other two interior angles.

∠DOC = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2

∠DOC = (53° + 46°) ÷ 2 = 99° ÷ 2 = 49.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 49.5°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

• In **quadrilateral ABCD**, ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 46°.

• OD and OC are the **angle bisectors** of ∠D and ∠C respectively, meeting at point O.

**Formula Used:**

• Sum of all interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°

• Sum of all interior angles of a **triangle** = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edbe167aa29f5227a05185edf26c9c1945dd016284f561749ed7874dc4965eac.png] 

**Calculations:**

In **quadrilateral ABCD**:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 53° + 46° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 99° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 360° − 99°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 261°

Since OD and OC are the **angle bisectors** of ∠D and ∠C respectively:

⇒ ∠ODC = ∠D ÷ 2

⇒ ∠OCD = ∠C ÷ 2

In **triangle DOC**:

⇒ ∠DOC + ∠ODC + ∠OCD = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + (∠D ÷ 2) + (∠C ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + 261° ÷ 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + 130.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC = 180° − 130.5°

⇒ ∠DOC = 49.5°

**Option Evaluation:**

• **Option (1) - 46.5°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠DOC is 49.5°.

• **Option (2) - 49.5°:** Correct, as it matches the calculated value of ∠DOC.

• **Option (3) - 60.5°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠DOC is 49.5°.

• **Option (4) - 44.5°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠DOC is 49.5°.

**∴ The correct answer is 49.5°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem in Quadrilaterals

For any quadrilateral ABCD, the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles (say ∠C and ∠D) is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles: ∠DOC = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2.

Opposite Angle Bisectors in Quadrilaterals

If the bisectors of opposite angles (say ∠A and ∠C) of a quadrilateral ABCD meet at a point, the angle between them is equal to half the difference of the other two opposite angles: θ = |∠B − ∠D| ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon

The sum of the interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by the formula: (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is always 360°.</p

questions.question: If (3, 2) are coordinates of the centroid of a triangle, whose vertices are (0, 4), (-2, 0) and (p, 2), then find the value of p.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **x-coordinate of the centroid** is the average of the **x-coordinates of the vertices**.

Sum of x-coordinates = 3 × Centroid x-coordinate

⇒ 0 + (−2) + p = 3 × 3

⇒ p − 2 = 9

⇒ p = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices of the triangle are A(0, 4), B(−2, 0), and C(p, 2). The **centroid** G is (3, 2).

**Formula Used:** The coordinates of the centroid G(x, y) of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) are given by:

x = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3

y = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fdd65cb360087255be7be0b649668e1e40af47bc8d732645f5f7e7f1e78638e7.png] 

**Calculations:**

For the **x-coordinate**:

⇒ 3 = (0 + (−2) + p) ÷ 3

⇒ 3 × 3 = −2 + p

⇒ 9 = p − 2

⇒ p = 9 + 2

⇒ p = 11

For the **y-coordinate** (Verification):

⇒ 2 = (4 + 0 + 2) ÷ 3

⇒ 2 = 6 ÷ 3

⇒ 2 = 2 (LHS = RHS)

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Centroid Definition

The **centroid** is the point of intersection of the three **medians** of a triangle (lines joining vertices to the midpoints of opposite sides).

Centroid Ratio Property

The centroid divides each median in the ratio **2 : 1**, with the larger part being closer to the vertex.

Area of Triangle (Coordinates)

Area = 1/2 |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|. This formula helps find the **area** using vertex coordinates.</p

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 32.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 4 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?

__Shortcut Trick__

In a **quadrilateral**, the angle formed by the **bisectors** of two adjacent angles is half the sum of the other two angles.

⇒ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2

⇒ 32.5° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 65°

⇒ Ratio ∠P : ∠Q = 4 : 9 ⇒ Total units = 13

⇒ 13 units = 65° ⇒ 1 unit = 5°

⇒ Difference = (9 − 4) × 5° = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠STR = 32.5°, Ratio of ∠P to ∠Q = 4 : 9.

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77275850ebcb689b901e884cde54cf6bb3482071cc281efdef2b75b9711a2c36.png] 

⇒ In ΔSTR, ∠TSR + ∠TRS + ∠STR = 180°

⇒ Since ST and RT are **angle bisectors**, ∠TSR = ∠S/2 and ∠TRS = ∠R/2

⇒ (∠S/2) + (∠R/2) + 32.5° = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 32.5° = 147.5°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 295°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 295° = 360° ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 65°

⇒ Let ∠P = 4x and ∠Q = 9x

⇒ 4x + 9x = 65° ⇒ 13x = 65° ⇒ x = 5°

⇒ Difference = 9x − 4x = 5x = 5 × 5° = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Property in Quadrilaterals

The angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles.

Sum of Interior Angles

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of interior angles is (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n=4), the sum is 360°.

Ratio and Difference

If two quantities are in ratio a : b and their sum is S, the difference between them is |a − b| × [S ÷ (a + b)].</p
